base_prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Redraw the FIRST reference image, an ORIGINAL Slay the Spire 1 card illustration, with very close fidelity to its SUBJECT, COMPOSITION, CAMERA, POSE, silhouette, contact point and movement direction. The user explicitly requests following the actual corresponding original card picture after rejecting invented compositions. FIRST IMAGE is mandatory composition/content reference. SECOND IMAGE is ONLY our approved illustration rendering style reference; do not copy its axe/hand/composition into new image. Produce ONE standalone square full-bleed card illustration, extend the first reference's background minimally to square without distorting subjects; remove any transparent black lower cutout and fill naturally. No text, numbers, border, title, card frame or UI. Rendering: hand-drawn dark comic, firm black outer contours, clean large flat color masses and HARD two-tone shadows, low-saturation slate blue-grey, iron grey, muted taupe and olive, pale clay highlights. Avoid excessive cracks or noisy scratch texture: human skin smooth and anatomically natural, leather leathery, metal solid. Preserve reference's clear background graphic rays; translate saturated background red to muted dark wine, orange effects to restrained amber and pale warm-grey. Keep adequate subject/background contrast, not muddy black. For visible protagonist only, adapt attire minimally to kiln apprentice: taupe work clothes, slate apron/leather straps, iron guards, dark hair and pale ceramic half-mask; do NOT disturb original pose or obstruct action. Natural flesh arms; no wood-grain skin, no accidental ceramic limbs unless specifically obvious from design. ONLY IF a sword actually appears in the FIRST reference, replace that sword with the original game's practical single-bladed woodcutting AXE. Preserve composition and action, adapt grip and impact so axe works anatomically and mechanically. CRITICAL: if original has NO weapon, draw NO WEAPON AT ALL; never add axes, floating axes or props from style reference. Second reference's axe gives correct construction. No swords anywhere, no sword-axe hybrids, no dagger guards. Each axe has one continuous forged steel cutting blade + eye + blunt poll on a wooden handle through eye. Cutting edge leads slashes; blunt poll leads pommel-style strikes. No added pottery or invented busy narrative. No gore. Detailed per-card invariant:

approved_common_base_prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. ONE square full-bleed card illustration, no frame, text, numbers, UI or watermark, for original game Ember's Kiln. Consistent approved starter-card style: dark hand-inked comic, bold near-black #1B1612 contours, thin internal structure lines, hard-edged flat cel shadows and large readable angular shapes. Cold desaturated slate #3A4554, iron grey #68665E, taupe #94826F, olive #35392C, pale flesh/clay #E0C1AC, deep purple-grey #332831. Tiny muted red #7E504E accent. Never pure white or saturated neon. Simplified sparse background, main action fills central 75%, readable at 128px. World is sunless ceramic land with kiln keepers as craftspeople, tools as weapons, pottery enemies instead of gore. If hero face appears: male kiln apprentice, dark swept-back shoulder-length hair, angular pointed pale ceramic half-mask covering forehead and eyes, human exposed lower face, taupe sleeveless work shirt, slate leather apron, riveted iron wrist guards, leather straps; right hand natural flesh, left hand pale ceramic. Correct anatomy, grip, tool construction and motion direction are essential. Wood grain ONLY on wooden tools, NEVER on skin. Every blade physically connected to its socket and shaft, cutting edge leads action. No random detached weapon parts. No horror, blood, photographic rendering, glossy 3D, excessive grunge, paper texture, oversaturated flames.
